application.when: surface=facade wall pixels on any grassland building; intensifies with min_age (honestly absent until chronicle wires age) and proximity-to-ground (always available); biased to splash-height band near the foundation and around the door_path approach
application.chanceOrDensity: always-on at low scalar (~0.15 baseline grime); scalar scales 0.15->0.8 with age; ground-band falloff means upper wall stays cleaner

objects.label: Wall Grime

coverage.scalar: driven by age|exposure 0-1 (handled-edge + ground-splash grime; honest-absent age contributes 0 until chronicle wires it, exposure/ground-proximity always available)

objects.biomeSkins: Universal on every biome's host wall material (grassland cob/fieldstone/timber_frame/wattle_daub; swaps to each biome's wall hosts elsewhere). Climate-default scalar bias: swamp/river/lake/shallow_water start higher (damp earth clings); desert/savanna/steppe shift the grime hue toward pale dust-tan; arctic/tundra/taiga suppress toward 0 (snow scours, frozen ground rarely splashes). Lit-multiplier raised in dark biomes (dense_forest, volcanic) so the multiply tint does not crush already-dim walls. No flora reskin. Drops on no biome.
objects.notes: Pure surface intensity, not a discrete object: a multiply tint riding the wall pixels with a gravity-up mask concentrating handled/splash grime near the base. No interact/destructible/light/content/attach because grime is a passive stain with no body, no yield, no hinge. wind_sway is absent (mechanism A decals never sway — anim is a property of suspension, which a painted-in tint lacks).

objects.label: Handprint & Wear Smudge

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1 localised to the door/threshold socket band (touch-wear); honest-absent age contributes 0 until chronicle wires it

objects.biomeSkins: Universal; the touch-wear band sits around the doorway on every biome's wall host. Wetter biomes (swamp/river) darken it; dry dusty biomes (desert/savanna/steppe) lighten and warm it. Suppressed near 0 on frozen biomes (arctic/tundra). Magical biomes (mystic) tint it faintly luminous-grey rather than recolouring it. No flora reskin, drops on no biome.
objects.notes: A patchy concentration of grime at hand-height around the threshold — still a coverage tint, not a sprite. All affordance components null for the same reason as wall_grime: it is a passive stain. Patchy falloff (no gravity direction) distinguishes it from the ground-rising wall_grime.

application.when: surface=facade/roof above a heat/smoke source — chimney flue, forge vent, or window of a hearth room; gated on building_role having an interior fire (smith strongest; inn/cottage moderate; granary/barn none) and on the chimney/vent socket existing
application.chanceOrDensity: present only where a smoke source exists; scalar 0.2->0.9 by role heat-intensity, plume-shaped rising from the source

objects.label: Chimney Plume Stain

coverage.scalar: driven by exposure (smoke-source heat-intensity, role-derived) 0-1; age contributes additively once a chronicle source exists (honest-absent for now)

objects.biomeSkins: Universal wherever a building has an interior fire; the dark plume tint rides each biome's chimney/eave host. Cold biomes (arctic/tundra/taiga/mountains) bias the scalar UP — fires burn constantly, plumes are heavier. Hot biomes (desert/savanna) bias DOWN. Volcanic tints the soot a warmer ember-grey; mystic faintly desaturates it toward ash-violet. No flora reskin, drops on no biome (the gate is the smoke source, not the biome).
objects.notes: A dark multiply plume rising from the flue/vent socket, fanning upward and thinning at the top (gravity-up, top falloff — the inverse of ground grime). source=procedural tint, not a sprite; the actual smoke PARTICLE belongs to D6 ground/air props, this is only the permanent stain it leaves. All affordances null: a stain has no hinge, no light of its own, no contents. light is null specifically because the GLOW belongs to the hearth/forge object, not to its soot mark.

objects.label: Forge Vent Scorch

coverage.scalar: driven by exposure (forge intensity, role=smith) 0-1; heavy near 1 by default on a working smithy

objects.biomeSkins: Universal but role-gated to smith/forge buildings; rides each biome's wall host above the forge vent. Heavier and warmer (ember-tinged) in volcanic; standard charcoal-black everywhere temperate. Cold biomes do not change it (a forge is a forge). No flora reskin, drops on no biome.
objects.notes: Role-glyph driven (only a smith building places it, biased dense by the forge glyph) — heavier and more localised than the household chimney plume. Same passive-stain rationale: every affordance null, no sway, multiply blend so it darkens rather than lights the wall.

application.when: surface=facade below a runoff edge (eave drip-line, sill underside, parapet); gated on min_wetness (biome+water-proximity, available 0-1 via terrain-suitability) and on a runoff edge existing above the streak
application.chanceOrDensity: scalar by wetness 0-1; vertical streaks seeded from eave/sill drip points, denser the wetter the biome

objects.label: Eave Drip Streak

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1 (biome + water-proximity, terrain-suitability derived — fully available, NOT honestly-absent)

objects.biomeSkins: Universal; rides each biome's wall host below the runoff edge. Wetness scalar is genuinely biome-driven: swamp/river/lake/shallow_water/ocean/deep_ocean/tropical_forest near max (constant runoff streaking); desert/savanna/steppe near 0 (drops on these in practice via the wetness gate, though the rule stays universal); arctic/tundra render it as frozen-pale icicle-stain rather than dark wet streak (climate-default state shift). Mystic faintly iridescent. No flora reskin.
objects.notes: Vertical gravity-DOWN streaks seeded at eave drip points and thinning downward (down direction, top falloff — strongest at the source). soft-light blend (darken-and-sheen, not flat multiply) reads as wet residue. This is the one D0 object whose scalar has a real sim source today (wetness), so it is not honestly-absent. All affordances null — a stain, not a vessel or light.

objects.label: Window-Sill Rundown

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1 (biome + water-proximity, terrain-suitability derived)

objects.biomeSkins: Universal, anchored under window sills on each biome's wall host. Same wetness biome bias as eave_drip_streak (high in wet biomes, near-0 dry). Frozen biomes render a pale rime-rundown. Mystic faintly luminous. No flora reskin, no hard drop (gated by wetness scalar).
objects.notes: A narrower twin of the eave streak, seeded at sill corners where rain sheds off the ledge. Same down/top/soft-light coverage shape, lower default scalar. All affordances null for the standard passive-stain reason.

application.when: surface=facade on the sun-exposed faces (south/west on a northern-hemisphere world); gated on exposure.sun from the surface descriptor and on min_age (paint/timber bleaches over years — honestly absent until chronicle age exists, so suppressed for now)
application.chanceOrDensity: scalar by sun-exposure x age; uniform desaturating wash on lit faces, none on shaded (north/east) faces

objects.label: Sun-Faced Fade

coverage.scalar: driven by exposure.sun x age 0-1; age component honestly-absent (0) until chronicle wires building age, exposure.sun fully available from the surface descriptor

objects.biomeSkins: Universal but the climate-default scalar is sun-driven: desert/savanna/steppe/volcanic bias HIGH (harsh sun bleaches hard, default sun_faded look even at low age); arctic/tundra/dense_forest/swamp bias LOW (weak or filtered sun). Facing-mask flips with no hemisphere data so it keys off the surface descriptor's exposure.sun rather than a literal compass face. Mystic adds a faint colour-shift instead of pure desaturation. No flora reskin, no hard drop.
objects.notes: The only facing-keyed D0 object: a desaturating soft-light wash applied uniformly to sun-exposed faces (facing:south via exposure.sun), absent on shaded faces. direction:none because UV bleaching is even across the lit face, not gravity-driven. Honestly-absent age means it is dialled to 0 today except where a biome's climate-default sun bias raises it. All affordances null — bleaching is a passive colour loss.

application.when: surface=facade with weatherable material (oxidising metal trim, greying timber, aging plaster); gated on material having a patina path and on min_age (oxidation is time — honestly absent until chronicle age, biased by wetness which IS available to accelerate it)
application.chanceOrDensity: scalar by age x wetness; broad patchy tone-shift across the field, concentrated on metal fittings and damp-held zones

objects.label: Weathered Patina

coverage.scalar: driven by age x wetness 0-1; age component honestly-absent (0) until chronicle, wetness component fully available so damp biomes still show patina

objects.biomeSkins: material-driven variant means the tint hue follows the host wall: grassland fieldstone greys, timber_frame oaks silver, cob earth-darkens, wattle_daub yellows. Across biomes the patina hue swaps with the wall host (rusty-brown on iron-fitted ocean/deep_ocean, verdigris green on copper-trimmed lake/river, salt-pale on coastal). Wet biomes (swamp/river/lake/shallow_water) bias the scalar UP (oxidation accelerates in damp). Frozen biomes bias DOWN. Volcanic tints toward sulphur-yellow; mystic toward an arcane blue-green patina. No flora reskin, no hard drop.
objects.notes: Variants driven by MATERIAL (not random) because the patina hue is a property of what the wall is made of — verdigris on copper, silver-grey on timber, etc. A broad patchy soft-light tone-shift, not a localised stain. age honestly-absent but wetness keeps it alive in damp biomes. All affordances null: patina is the material slowly recolouring itself, no body/light/yield/hinge.

application.when: surface=masonry/plaster/cob foundation and lower wall (salt blooms where damp wicks up through stone/earth); gated on material being porous-mineral (fieldstone/cob/wattle_daub plinth — NOT bare timber) and on min_wetness (rising damp, available 0-1)
application.chanceOrDensity: scalar by wetness 0-1; pale crystalline bloom rising a short way up from the damp-course, capped low on the wall

objects.label: Rising-Damp Salt Bloom

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1 (rising-damp, biome + water-proximity, terrain-suitability derived — available, not honestly-absent)

objects.biomeSkins: Universal on porous-mineral hosts; grassland applies it to fieldstone/cob/wattle_daub bases (NOT pure timber_frame, which lacks the wicking mineral plinth — the material gate handles that). Coastal/marine biomes (ocean/deep_ocean/shallow_water/beach) bias HIGH and warm the bloom toward salt-white sea-crust; swamp/river/lake also high. Desert renders an alkali/efflorescent crust that is genuinely strong (mineral ground) even though dry — a notable exception where the climate-default RAISES it. Arctic/tundra render it as pale frost-rime. Mystic gives it a faint crystalline shimmer. No flora reskin.
objects.notes: A pale ADDITIVE-feeling crystalline bloom (soft-light lightens the surface, the only D0 object that brightens rather than darkens) rising a capped distance up from the damp-course. up/bottom mask = strongest at the base, fading upward — the salt-deposit inverse of the gravity-down water streak. Material-driven variants and a porous-mineral material gate (no timber). Wetness has a real source so it is not honestly-absent. All affordances null.

application.when: surface=lowest facade/foundation band; gated on min_wetness (rain-splash needs wet ground, available 0-1) and proximity to the door_path/traffic approach where churned mud splashes highest; ground-band only
application.chanceOrDensity: scalar by wetness x ground-traffic; dense earthy splatter in the bottom ~tile band, tapering sharply upward

objects.label: Rain-Splash Mud

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1 (biome + water-proximity, terrain-suitability derived); ground-traffic near the door raises it where available

objects.biomeSkins: Universal; the splatter hue follows each biome's ground colour — grassland earth-brown, beach/coastal sandy-tan, volcanic ash-grey, swamp peat-black, desert dust-ochre. Wetness gate makes it heavy in swamp/river/lake/tropical_forest and near-0 in desert/savanna/steppe and on frozen arctic/tundra (mud freezes — climate-default near 0, effectively dropped via the gate). Mystic shifts the splatter faintly luminescent. No flora reskin.
objects.notes: The hardest-edged, lowest D0 band: dense multiply splatter in the bottom tile that taper sharply (up direction, bottom falloff — strongest at ground, gone by knee height). Distinct from wall_grime (broader, softer, higher) by its tight ground confinement and traffic-near-door bias. Wetness is a real sim source. All affordances null — a splash mark is a passive stain with no body, light, contents, or hinge.

fields.crossBiomeNotes: D0 weathering is the cheapest, most universal dressing field: every object is a procedural coverage tint riding the existing wall/roof/foundation pixels (mechanism A) with zero new PixelLab assets, so it specializes across all 21 biomes purely by (a) climate-default SCALAR bias per object (wet biomes raise water/efflorescence/mud/grime; dry hot biomes raise sun-fade and suppress mud; frozen biomes suppress most stains and re-skin water/salt as pale rime/frost; volcanic warms soot/patina; mystic adds faint luminance/iridescence), (b) HOST-material hue follow (patina and salt blooms swap their tint to whatever the biome wall material is — verdigris copper, silver timber, salt-white coastal, sulphur volcanic), and (c) GROUND-colour follow (mud splatter takes the local soil/sand/ash colour). Only two real semantic sources exist today: wetness (terrain-suitability, fully available — drives water streaks, efflorescence, mud) and exposure.sun + heat-source role (drive sun-fade and soot). age/wealth/maintenance are HONESTLY ABSENT: every age-gated scalar (grime accrual, sun-fade, patina, handprint wear) is dialled to 0 from age and contributes only via its available co-driver (wetness, sun, or biome climate-default) until the settlement chronicle wires building age into dressingContext. No object carries interact/destructible/light/content/attach because weathering is passive surface intensity, and none carries wind_sway because painted-in decals never suspend. Per-biome multiplicative size has no meaning for cover-fit objects; the per-biome tuner instead scales each object's default coverage scalar (reusing field-tuning.js).

fields.defaultProvenance: procedural (cracks/wear/rot/rust coverage) + sprite chips (missing tiles / patches)

application.when: biome:any · surface_type:any solid wall (plaster/daub/cob/stone/timber-frame infill) · min_age present in dressingContext · settlement_tier:any · scalar rises with age and (for cob/daub) with wetness
application.chanceOrDensity: coverage-driven: cracks begin appearing above age ~0.35, density scales 0..1 with age; gated OFF entirely while age is honestly-absent (no faked aging)

objects.label: Hairline Plaster Cracks

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1 (begins ~0.35)

objects.biomeSkins: Material host swap selects the crack palette: warm-cream lime daub (wattle_daub/timber_frame infill), earthen ochre (cob), grey lime mortar (fieldstone joint cracks). Cold biomes (taiga/tundra/arctic/mountains) add freeze-thaw widening → scalar multiplier ×1.4 from wetness. Mystic/volcanic re-skin the crack line to a faint emissive seam handled by the lit-multiplier on D0, not here. Dry biomes (desert/steppe/savanna) bias to fine sun-shrinkage crazing rather than structural cracks (textureVariant index biased low).
objects.notes: Pure intensity surface decal — no discrete art, no states beyond base. A coverage scalar + patchy mask painted into the wall bitmap via soft-light/multiply (drawWallDecals). No wind_sway (nothing suspended), no interact, no light. Honestly absent until a sim age source exists; the rule engine skips it when dressingContext.age is null.

objects.label: Structural Settlement Crack

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1 (begins ~0.6, sparse)

objects.biomeSkins: Stone biomes (fieldstone host, hills, mountains) widen the crack into a mortar-joint step-crack following the courses; cob/daub biomes show a single tapering vertical fissure rising from the plinth. Wet biomes (swamp/river/lake/ocean) accelerate via subsidence → scalar starts earlier (~0.45). Magical biomes do not specialize this object (no enchanted fractures).
objects.notes: Heavier, sparse single-fracture coverage seeded to rise from the foundation course (mask direction up, falloff bottom) where settlement stress concentrates. Adds a faint cast-shadow lip for depth. Still a coverage surface (no sprite), age-gated, no other affordances.

application.when: biome:any · surface_type:plaster/render/painted/fired-tile faces · min_age present · exposure:high (sun+wet faces spall first) · scalar rises with age and wetness
application.chanceOrDensity: coverage-driven: flaked patches accumulate 0..1 with age, biased onto sun/wet-exposed faces

objects.label: Flaking Lime-Wash / Paint

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1

objects.biomeSkins: Reveals the substrate beneath the wash: warm earthen ochre under cob, grey daub under wattle_daub/timber_frame infill. Sun-faded biomes (desert/steppe/savanna/beach) bias the flaking heavily onto the south/sun face (facing south) and raise the scalar (×1.3). Cold/wet biomes (taiga/tundra/swamp) drive frost-spall instead — same coverage, mask falloff bottom where moisture wicks. Magical biomes do not specialize.
objects.notes: Coverage decal that lightens/reveals substrate where the surface coat has flaked. Soft-light blend so it reads as removed coating, not added dirt (that is D0). Sun-facing bias (facing south). No discrete states, no interact/light; age+exposure driven, honestly absent without age.

objects.label: Spalled Brick / Fired-Tile Face

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1 (freeze-thaw)

objects.biomeSkins: Applies where a building has a fired clay_tile roof skirt or brick course; in grassland that is the fieldstone+clay_tile pairing. Frost biomes (taiga/tundra/arctic/mountains) drive the scalar hard via wetness freeze-thaw. Dry/warm biomes mostly skip it (scalar floors near 0). Volcanic adds a heat-crazed variant via material-driven textureVariant.
objects.notes: Pocked spalling of a hard fired face, wetness/freeze-thaw driven rather than age. Material-driven variant (which fired surface). Coverage only; pairs with stone wear. No suspension/interact/light.

application.when: biome:any · surface_type:stone (fieldstone host, dressed quoins, foundation plinth) · min_age present · exposure:wet/sun · scalar rises with age and wetness
application.chanceOrDensity: coverage-driven: rounding/pitting/runnels accumulate 0..1, concentrated on the foundation course and weather faces

objects.label: Weather-Pitted Stone

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1

objects.biomeSkins: Material host selects the stone palette (grey-tan glacial fieldstone in grassland; harder slate in hills/mountains erodes slower → scalar ×0.6; soft coral/tabby in beach erodes faster → ×1.4). Wet biomes (ocean/river/lake/swamp) deepen the pitting via salt/spray. Mystic/volcanic do not specialize this object.
objects.notes: Surface micro-pitting and rounding of dressed/field stone — a slow age-driven coverage with a depth shadow so edges read softened. Material-driven texture. No discrete states (erosion is continuous), no interact/light/suspension.

objects.label: Eroded Drip Runnels

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1

objects.biomeSkins: Strongest in wet biomes (river/lake/ocean/swamp/shallow_water → scalar ×1.5) below roof eaves and sills where runoff concentrates; nearly absent in desert/steppe/savanna (scalar floors). Cold biomes add an ice-glaze variant only via D0 wetness sheen, not here.
objects.notes: Vertical eroded channels carved by roof/sill runoff — gravity-directed coverage (direction down, falloff bottom). Distinct from D0 water-stain (which is a tint, not removed stone): this erodes the substrate. Wetness driven, no age dependence, so it can render even while age is absent. No suspension/interact/light.

application.when: biome:any · surface_type:exposed timber (timber_frame studs/braces, plank cladding, sills, eaves boards) · min_age present · exposure:wet · scalar rises with age and wetness
application.chanceOrDensity: coverage-driven: softening/greying/punky rot accumulates 0..1, concentrated low (ground-contact) and on wet faces

objects.label: Greyed & Punky Timber

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1, amplified by wetness

objects.biomeSkins: Applies to any host with exposed wood: timber_frame studs and the cob/daub eave cap in grassland. Wet biomes (swamp/river/lake/ocean/shallow_water/tropical_forest/dense_forest) drive the scalar hard (×1.6) and bias the shaded north face. Dry biomes (desert/steppe/savanna/arctic/tundra) show sun-checking/silvering instead of wet rot — same coverage, facing south, drier palette via textureVariant. Mystic adds no special rot.
objects.notes: Ground-up wet rot: timber greys and goes punky from the foundation contact upward (mask direction up, falloff bottom) and on the shaded damp north face. Soft-light tint that desaturates and darkens the wood. Age+wetness driven, honestly absent without age. No suspension/interact/light; if rot fully consumes a board that becomes a missing_tiles gap object, not a state here.

objects.label: Dry-Rot Crumble Patch

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1

objects.biomeSkins: Localized crumbling cube-rot patches in older timber, strongest in humid temperate biomes (forest/grassland/river). Arid biomes show this as insect-bored sun-checking instead (textureVariant biased). Magical biomes do not specialize.
objects.notes: Cubical dry-rot patches that crumble the timber surface — patchy coverage with a depth shadow so the patch reads recessed. Age driven. A late-stage patch that has eaten through becomes a missing_tiles gap. No suspension/interact/light.

application.when: biome:any · surface_type:exposed ironwork (nail rows, strap hinges, brackets, ties, banding) · min_age present · exposure:wet · scalar rises with age and wetness
application.chanceOrDensity: coverage-driven: rust bloom + drip-streaks accumulate 0..1 around metal fixtures, strongest in wet/salt biomes

objects.label: Iron Rust Bloom & Streak

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1, amplified by age

objects.biomeSkins: Anchored to wherever the base building exposes ironwork (nailed plank/timber_frame in grassland). Salt-spray biomes (ocean/deep_ocean/shallow_water/beach) drive the scalar hardest (×1.8) with deep orange bleed; dry biomes (desert/steppe/savanna) barely rust (×0.4, paler bloom). Volcanic adds a sulfur-stained variant via textureVariant; mystic may swap iron for a verdigris bronze patina palette (still a coverage tint, lit-multiplier handled by D0).
objects.notes: Rust bloom centered on metal fixtures with downward drip-streaks bleeding onto the wall below (direction down, falloff bottom). Wetness driven primarily so it can render without age. Multiply blend keeps the orange staining the substrate. No suspension/interact/light — the metal body itself (hinge/bracket) is a D3 prop; this is only its corrosion.

application.when: biome:any · surface_type:roof courses, eaves boards, plank gaps · min_age present (advanced age/neglect) OR post-destruction delta · settlement_tier:any (poorer/abandoned skew higher)
application.chanceOrDensity: sparse discrete chips: 0-6 missing/displaced pieces per roof, density rising with age; each is a small sprite hole placed on a roof-course or eave socket

objects.label: Missing / Slipped Roof Course Piece
objects.biomeSkins: Material-driven variant matches the roof material catalog: thatch (a torn dark gap + loose straw), wood_shingle (a missing shake showing batten), clay_tile (a slipped/absent pantile showing dark underlay), turf_sod (a bare soil scar). Each biome's roof set maps to its own variant — e.g. ocean cedar_shake, river slate, lake birch_bark. Poor/abandoned settlement tier raises density. Snow biomes (arctic/tundra/taiga) partly hide gaps under snow cap (content axis on the roof base, not here).
objects.notes: A small PixelLab sprite painted into the roof bitmap at a course/eave socket — a real hole that darkens to underlay (shadow code effect for the recessed cavity). DESTRUCTIBLE because it represents structural loss and can be widened: a destruction interaction writes an object-permanence delta (broken_state=destroyed, dropping a tile shard on the ground below). No light/interact/content/suspension. wind_sway never applies (a hole is not suspended cloth).

objects.label: Sprung / Missing Wall Plank
objects.biomeSkins: Applies to plank/board-clad and timber_frame walls (the grassland timber_frame and any board host). Variant matches the wall material: a sprung honey-oak board (forest/grassland), a tar-blackened plank (river/ocean), a bleached driftwood board (beach/shallow_water). Wet biomes raise density (rot-driven). Stone-only hosts (fieldstone, cob, coral) drop this object — a monolithic wall does not lose planks (see biomeApplicability note in code via host check).
objects.notes: A vertical 1x2 sprite of a missing or hanging wall board showing the dark interior gap behind (shadow). DESTRUCTIBLE: can be torn fully away, writing a delta and dropping a splinter on the ground. Host-gated to board/timber walls at resolve time. No light/interact/content; no suspension so no wind_sway.

application.when: biome:any · co-located with prior damage (a missing-tile/gap/crack socket) · min_age present (a repair implies a prior fault) · settlement_tier:any (occupied/maintained skew higher — patches mean someone still tends the building)
application.chanceOrDensity: sparse discrete chips placed ON or beside a damage socket: 0-4 patches per building; presence signals an inhabited, mended structure rather than an abandoned one

objects.label: Nailed Board Patch
objects.biomeSkins: A mismatched salvaged board nailed over a gap; variant picks a fresh-vs-aged contrast against the host (raw light board over weathered wall, or tarred board over a plank wall). `weathered` state lets an old patch grey out and itself become damage. Every biome reuses its local salvage timber palette (driftwood in beach/ocean, bamboo offcut in tropical_forest, dark-stained board in dense_forest). Stone biomes use a mortar-smear patch variant instead (textureVariant) since boards do not patch ashlar.
objects.notes: A small PixelLab sprite of a crude nailed-on repair board, sitting slightly proud (drop shadow). A 'weathered' wear state — orthogonal to the patch identity — lets it age into its own damage. DESTRUCTIBLE (can be pried off, dropping a splinter + writing a delta). No light/interact/content; rigid, not suspended, so no wind_sway. Placement is co-gated to an existing damage socket so a patch always reads as a repair of a real fault, never decoration on a pristine wall.

objects.label: Fresh Daub / Mortar Fill

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1 (fresh=light contrast, weathered=blends in)

objects.biomeSkins: A smeared infill of fresh lime daub / mortar over a crack or spall, lighter and smoother than the aged wall around it. Host-matched: cream lime (wattle_daub/timber_frame infill), earthen mud (cob), grey mortar (fieldstone joints). Wet biomes weather the patch faster (scalar climbs quicker). Desert/steppe sun-bleach it pale. Mystic/volcanic do not specialize. Hybrid = a small patch decal mask blended over the wall (no separate sprite chip needed), so it rides the bitmap like the other surface decals.
objects.notes: A repair smear that is brighter/smoother than the surrounding aged surface, fading toward the wall tone as it weathers (age-driven contrast). Hybrid: implemented as a localized coverage patch (soft-light) rather than a hard sprite, since fill conforms to the wall. NOT destructible (it is the same material as the wall — destroying it just reverts to the underlying crack/spall). No light/interact/content/suspension. Co-gated to a damage socket like the board patch.

fields.crossBiomeNotes: D1 specializes across the 21 biomes almost entirely by (a) MATERIAL HOST swap — each coverage decal recolours to the wall/roof material catalog already defined in building-materials.json (cob earthen ochre, wattle_daub/timber_frame cream lime, fieldstone grey mortar/grey-tan stone), and each sprite chip variant maps to that biome's roof/wall material set — and (b) CLIMATE multipliers on the coverage scalar: wet biomes (ocean/deep_ocean/shallow_water/beach/river/lake/swamp/tropical_forest) amplify wood_rot, rust, water-runnel erosion and spalling; cold/freeze-thaw biomes (taiga/tundra/arctic/mountains) amplify cracks, tile-spalling and stone pitting; arid biomes (desert/steppe/savanna) suppress rot/rust/erosion but raise sun-checking and paint-flaking on the sun face. Two cross-cutting RULES the design doc mandates: (1) every age-driven object is HONESTLY ABSENT until a sim age/maintenance source exists in dressingContext — the rule engine skips it rather than faking aging; wetness-driven objects (water-runnel erosion, rust, spall) CAN render now because wetness is derivable from biome+water-proximity. (2) damage is presentation but the two destructible sprite-chip objects (missing tiles, plank gaps, board patches) write real object-permanence deltas when widened/removed, never a faked break. No D1 object is suspended/cloth, so wind_sway never applies to this entire field (all anim=static); none are light sources (no light component); none are vessels (no content); none compose children (no attach). Magical biomes (mystic/volcanic) do NOT invent enchanted damage — they reuse the same coverage with a palette/lit-multiplier handled in D0, keeping D1 honest structural decay everywhere.

application.when: biome=grassland on any wall surface (D0/D1 host) where exposure.wet>=0.35 OR exposure.shade>=0.5; biased to the north (shaded) face and to the wall-base band where ground damp wicks up; intensity = a wetness scalar (water-proximity + biome humidity, from terrain-suitability 0-1). min_age would deepen coverage but age is honestly absent (no sim source) so coverage is driven by wetness+shade alone today.
application.chanceOrDensity: coverage scalar 0-1 per wall surface; present (>0) on ~55% of north-facing grassland wall surfaces, ~15% of south-facing, scaling with wetness

objects.label: Moss film (coverage growth)

coverage.scalar: driven by wetness 0-1 (water-proximity + humidity); age would deepen it but is honestly absent

objects.biomeSkins: Surface field — specializes by the host wall MATERIAL it rides (grassland: cob/fieldstone/timber_frame/wattle_daub) plus per-biome climate default for the wetness scalar: dense_forest/swamp/tropical_forest = wetness clamped HIGH (lush emerald moss is the climate-default, near-full coverage even south-facing); forest/lake/river = moderate; grassland/hills/steppe/savanna = moderate-low, north-face only; desert/volcanic/beach/arctic/tundra = dropped (no moss skin, replaced by lichen/sand-crust). Flora-reskin: tropical biomes use a deeper viridian textureVariant set; mystic uses a faint emissive moonmoss tint (lit-multiplier handled in D2_lichen's mystic skin rather than here). Drop condition: humidity<0.2 OR permafrost biome.
objects.notes: A SURFACE field, not a discrete object: per the design's surface rule it is intensity-driven (a coverage scalar + gravity/facing mask) painted soft-light INTO the wall bitmap, never a placed sprite with wear states. Mask direction=up + falloff=bottom because moss creeps upward from the damp ground band; facing=north because shade keeps it from drying. wind_sway is absent — moss is fused to the surface, not suspended, so per the calibration rule it gets no sway. No interact/light/content — it is inert living film.

objects.label: Moss cushion patch (raised sprite tufts)
objects.biomeSkins: Sprite half of the moss hybrid — placed only where the coverage film already exceeds ~0.6, so it never appears on a dry wall. dense_forest/swamp: larger cushions, deeper viridian, +1 variant of mushroom-studded cushion; grassland/forest: standard green; mystic: faint glow rim shares D2_lichen's lit-multiplier; dropped wherever moss_film is dropped.
objects.notes: The 3D-reading cushions that sit ON TOP of the flat coverage film to give the moss volume and a small ground-shadow at its lower edge. It is a sprite (the patch + shadow), but it is GATED by the coverage scalar of moss_film in the same category — the hybrid pattern named in the design (patch + coverage-scatter). Discrete sprite, so it carries a single base state, not the coverage sub-grain; it is removed (claim freed) rather than damaged. No sway (clings to wall), no light, no interact.

application.when: biome=grassland on bare stone/earthen wall surfaces (fieldstone, cob) — lichen prefers mineral/lime hosts over painted plaster or timber; tolerates LOW wetness (exposure.wet>=0.1) so it colonizes drier, sunnier walls where moss cannot; intensity = a slow age scalar in principle, but age is honestly absent → driven by a stable per-surface random + a mild wetness term. No facing preference (grows sun or shade).
application.chanceOrDensity: coverage scalar 0-1; faint presence (0.1-0.4) on ~70% of grassland fieldstone/cob surfaces, sparse on timber/plaster

objects.label: Crustose lichen mottle (coverage)

coverage.scalar: driven by age 0-1 (slow colonization); age honestly absent → stable per-surface random + mild wetness term substitutes

objects.biomeSkins: Pure-procedural coverage mottle (no asset) tinted to the host stone. Climate-default tint shifts per biome: grassland/hills = grey-green + ochre rosettes; arctic/tundra/mountains = pale grey-white map-lichen (the climate DEFAULT here — replaces moss, which is dropped in cold-dry biomes); desert/volcanic/steppe = rust-orange and black desert-varnish crust at low coverage; swamp/tropical = mostly suppressed (moss out-competes it). mystic: a faint luminescent cyan lichen with a small lit-multiplier feeding the GL lighting pass. Universal because crust lichen colonizes nearly any stone in any climate, only the palette changes.
objects.notes: A SURFACE field rendered as a flat soft-light tint mottle into the wall bitmap — the cheapest D2 effect, zero assets, proves the coverage/mask path with no PixelLab cost. mask.direction=none (lichen ignores gravity, unlike moss) and falloff=patchy with facing=any (grows sun or shade). Intensity-driven coverage, never discrete states. No sway/light/interact/content — inert mineral crust. Its honest age-absence is the canonical example of a surface whose true driver (slow age) has no sim source yet.

application.when: biome=grassland; one or more vine roots seeded at the wall-base (foundation course) of a wall surface, growing upward; favored on shaded/damp faces (exposure.shade>=0.4 OR exposure.wet>=0.3) and strongly biased on by the 'abandoned'/'overgrown' building role (identity kit D7 turns this category up). Maturity of the climb would be an age scalar; age honestly absent → climb height = min(rule_cap, wall_top) with a per-root random fraction, NOT a faked age.
application.chanceOrDensity: 0-3 vine roots per qualifying wall surface; ~20% of ordinary grassland walls carry at least one vine, ~85% of abandoned-role walls

objects.label: Ivy stem segment (spline piece)
objects.biomeSkins: The spine piece of the vine spline. Flora-reskin per biome to the biome's climbing plant: grassland/forest = green ivy; tropical_forest/swamp = thick liana with aerial roots (+1 fork density); dense_forest = dark mossy creeper; mystic = faint glowing tendril (shares a lit-multiplier with ivy_leaf_cluster); desert/volcanic/arctic/tundra = DROPPED (replaced by climbing_roots or nothing — no leafy vine in arid/frozen biomes); savanna/steppe = sparse dry creeper, fewer leaf clusters. Material host is irrelevant (vine rides over any wall).
objects.notes: A GROW-fit spline piece: the placement engine generates a path up the wall from the foundation root, then tiles segment pieces along it, branching at forks and stopping at min(rule_cap, wall_top), routing AROUND aperture blocked-zones. wind_sway is ABSENT despite being foliage — the design's rule is that sway is a property of SUSPENSION; ivy is gripped to the wall surface, not hanging, so it does not sway (its leaf_cluster tips get a tiny shader flutter via the leaf object, not full wind_sway). Destructible because a vine can be torn down (writes an object-permanence delta + leaf-litter debris). Built from pieces (segment/fork/leaf_cluster/root_base) per the design's vine recipe.

objects.label: Ivy branch fork (spline junction)
objects.biomeSkins: Junction piece placed by the spline assembler wherever the generated path branches; same flora-reskin + drop rules as ivy_segment. tropical/swamp lianas fork more often (denser canopy on the wall); dry biomes fork rarely.
objects.notes: A kit piece, not an independent placement — the spline assembler inserts a fork sprite at branch nodes so the vine reads as one organism rather than parallel stems. grow-fit. No sway (clings), no light. Shares the vine's destructible behavior (part of the same torn-down delta).

objects.label: Ivy leaf cluster (spline tip foliage)
objects.biomeSkins: Leafy mass clustered along the stem and at growth tips; the most visible part of the vine. Flora-reskin to biome bloom/leaf catalog: grassland green ivy; tropical broad glossy liana leaves; dense_forest dark serrated leaves; mystic faintly luminous foliage (lit-multiplier into the lighting pass); flowering variant (+1) in spring-coded grassland/forest. Dropped wherever ivy_segment is dropped.
objects.notes: The ONE vine piece that animates: its loose leaf tips are effectively suspended at the edge of the clinging stem, so per the suspension rule it carries a gentle wind_sway (realized as a small shader-sway perturbation of the leaf edges, NOT a full bake — frame budget per the motion taxonomy's wind_sway). The stem pieces (segment/fork) stay static because they grip the wall. Destructible (stripping leaves leaves a bare_stem). Built as part of the grow spline.

objects.label: Ivy root base (spline anchor)
objects.biomeSkins: The woody base mass where the vine emerges from the ground at the foundation course; one per vine root. Thicker/gnarled in tropical (liana boles) and dense_forest; thin in dry-biome creepers; dropped with the rest of the vine in arid/frozen biomes.
objects.notes: The spline's start anchor, fixed at the wall-base — the assembler grows the segment/fork/leaf chain UP from here. fit=fixed (it does not stretch). It carries the ground-contact shadow so the vine reads as rooted. Cutting the root base destroys the whole vine (the spline above it is removed) — the heaviest destructible of the group, emitting woody-stem debris.

application.when: biome=grassland on earthen/stone walls (cob, fieldstone) adjacent to large trees or on the damp/shaded lower wall; stronger on the abandoned-role building (roots reclaim the structure). Driven by wetness (exposure.wet>=0.3) and proximity-to-tree; would deepen with age (honestly absent). Distinct from ivy: woody, leafless, hugging crevices and mortar joints from the base upward, rarely above mid-wall.
application.chanceOrDensity: 0-2 root systems per qualifying lower wall surface; ~10% of ordinary grassland walls, ~50% of abandoned-role walls near trees

objects.label: Climbing root tendril (spline piece)
objects.biomeSkins: Woody leafless tendril following mortar joints. Climate-reskin: grassland/forest pale woody roots; dense_forest/swamp dark wet roots with rootlets (+fork density); volcanic charred crawling roots; mystic pulsing glow-veined roots (lit-multiplier); desert/steppe dry cracked roots, sparse; arctic/tundra DROPPED (no woody climbers in permafrost). Hosts on stone/earth walls only (will not appear over fresh plaster).
objects.notes: A spline field like ivy but with NO leaf pieces — pure woody tendrils that branch and hug the wall, so the whole assembly is static (no suspended foliage → no wind_sway at all, the cleanest application of the suspension rule). grow-fit, assembled from tendril + fork pieces rooted at the base, capped at mid-wall. Destructible (snapping a root writes a delta + splinter debris). Reuses the same spline-assembly engine as ivy, validating it for a leafless climber.

objects.label: Climbing root fork (spline junction)
objects.biomeSkins: Branch junction for the root spline; same reskin/drop rules as root_tendril. Wetter biomes fork more (denser root mat).
objects.notes: Kit junction piece inserted at spline branch nodes; not independently placed. grow-fit, static, shares the root system's destructible delta. Keeps the climber reading as one organism.

application.when: biome=grassland; small weeds/grass tufts rooting in cracks, mortar gaps, and on window-sill and string-course ledges where wind-blown soil collects; favored on damp/neglected walls (exposure.wet>=0.25) and turned up by the abandoned role. Lifecycle would track season/age (partly absent) → uses the F2-flora visual vocabulary (seedling/normal/wilting/dead) where a season cue exists, else normal only.
application.chanceOrDensity: per-ledge/crack socket; ~30% of grassland sill/ledge sockets carry a tuft, ~70% on abandoned-role walls

objects.label: Crack grass tuft
objects.biomeSkins: A small living tuft rooting in wall cracks. Flora-reskin to the biome's small-flora catalog (the F2 archetypes): grassland = grass + cornflower/daisy sprig; desert = dry tuft / sand_verbena; tundra/arctic = moss_campion cushion (reduced wind_sway); swamp = rush sprig; mystic = faintly glowing tuft (lit-multiplier); savanna/steppe = dry bunchgrass. Climate-default state: arid biomes default to 'wilting', cold biomes shorter/sparser, lush biomes 'normal'. Universal (some weed colonizes cracked walls in every biome) but the species swaps wholesale.
objects.notes: A small SPRITE rooted in a crack/ledge socket — unlike moss/lichen this is a discrete plant, so it DOES take the F2 flora lifecycle states (seedling/normal/wilting/dead, per the asset-state taxonomy default map) rather than a coverage scalar. It carries wind_sway because the loose blades ARE suspended/free at the tip (suspension rule satisfied) — a shader-sway flutter, frame count per the wind_sway motion-taxonomy entry. Ground-contact shadow at the root. Destructible = simply transitions to dead / is removed (claim freed); no debris. No light/content/interact.

categories.label: Fungal shelf

application.when: biome=grassland on DAMP TIMBER wall hosts only (timber_frame, wattle_daub timbers, plank sills) where exposure.wet>=0.5 — bracket fungi need rotting wood, so this is gated to wet timber, not stone/cob; strongly favored on the abandoned/decayed building role (the design's abandoned identity = boards+heavy vines+moss+rot). Decay-stage would drive it (age/maintenance absent) → gated on wetness + timber host + abandoned-role bias only.
application.chanceOrDensity: per damp-timber socket; ~8% of wet grassland timber sockets, ~45% on abandoned-role wet timber walls

categories.biomeApplicability: only:[grassland, forest, dense_forest, tropical_forest, taiga, swamp, lake, river, beach, hills, mountains, mystic]

objects.label: Bracket / shelf fungus
objects.biomeSkins: A stacked shelf of bracket fungus clinging to rotting timber. Flora-reskin to biome fungus: grassland/forest tan-brown turkeytail brackets; dense_forest/swamp larger darker shelves (+1 variant); tropical bright orange shelf; taiga pale birch-polypore; mystic GLOWING bioluminescent shelf — here the lit-multiplier flips this object's light component ON in the mystic skin (a soft green glow, color/radius small, diurnal off i.e. always-on, no flicker) feeding the GL lighting pass, the one biome where the otherwise-dark fungus emits. Volcanic/desert/arctic/tundra/savanna/steppe = DROPPED (the category is only:[...] — no rotting-timber fungus in arid, frozen, or treeless-host biomes).
objects.notes: A discrete SPRITE shelf fungus on damp rotting wood — MATTER-with-decay-tail per the taxonomy (no full life spine), so its states are base / mossy_overgrown (the decay progression) / dead, NOT the flora seedling ramp and NOT a coverage scalar. No wind_sway: a rigid shelf fused to the timber is the textbook NON-suspended case (contrast the awning rule). Destructible (knocking it off emits fungus fragments + delta). light is null in all biomes EXCEPT the mystic skin, where the biomeSkins lit-multiplier turns on a bioluminescent glow — the design's 'magical variant for mystic' rule. No interact/content.

fields.crossBiomeNotes: D2 is the LIVING-SURFACE field: it specializes across the 20 non-grassland biomes along three levers from the design. (1) Material host: every object rides whatever wall material that biome supplies (building-materials.json hosts) — moss/lichen tint to the stone, vines/roots/fungus ignore the host but gate on stone-vs-timber-vs-earth. (2) Climate-default coverage/state: the wetness and shade scalars are clamped per biome so the climate default is honest — dense_forest/swamp/tropical = lush near-full moss + frequent vines/fungus; forest/lake/river = moderate; grassland/hills/savanna/steppe = light, north-face-biased; desert/volcanic/beach = moss DROPPED and replaced by rust/varnish LICHEN crust + dry creepers; arctic/tundra/mountains = pale map-lichen is the default (moss and leafy vines dropped); mystic = faint emissive variants (glow-moss, luminous lichen, glowing liana tips, bioluminescent bracket fungus) via the lit-multiplier feeding the GL lighting pass; volcanic = charred roots, ash-crust, no foliage. (3) Flora-reskin: vines/weeds/fungus swap species wholesale to the biome's F2-flora / bloom catalog while keeping the same spline/socket machinery. Two render mechanisms coexist in this field: surfaces (moss_film, lichen) are COVERAGE sub-grain decals (no discrete states, intensity-driven, soft-light into the wall bitmap); placed growth (ivy, roots, weeds, fungus) are spline-assembled or socket-placed sprites with real states. The suspension rule is applied precisely: nothing here sways EXCEPT the loose leaf tips (ivy_leaf_cluster) and free grass blades (crack_grass_tuft), because everything else is fused/gripped to the surface. Age/maintenance/decay-stage are the TRUE drivers of most of this growth and have NO sim source yet — they are honestly absent everywhere, substituted by wetness + shade + facing + the abandoned building-role bias, never faked.

fields.defaultProvenance: pixellab (sprite); hybrid where a prop is lit, swaying, or strung

application.when: biome:grassland; building_role in {inn, tavern, shop, market_stall, bakery, butcher, general_store}; socket=above_door or shopfront window run on the ground floor (floor=0); commercial/hospitality frontage only
avoid: above upper-floor apertures until vertical sockets render
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.7 on commercial frontage sockets, else 0; one awning per shopfront span

objects.label: Striped Cloth Awning
objects.biomeSkins: Cloth host swaps weave/palette per biome: desert/savanna → sun-bleached ochre canvas (climate-default state sun_faded), swamp/tropical_forest → mildew-stained linen, arctic/tundra/taiga → oiled heavy canvas + climate-default snow dusting on the upper fold, volcanic → ash-grey scorched edges, mystic → shimmering enchanted weave (subtle emissive added). Lit-multiplier n/a (no light). Drops on biomes with no cloth-trade settlements (deep_ocean platforms keep only oiled_canvas variant).
objects.notes: wind_sway applies because it is suspended cloth (the calibration rule: anim is a property of SUSPENSION, not the category). 'rolled' is the stowed content-less state, not a wear state. Destructible because fabric is fragile; broken_state degrades to 'tattered' and writes an object-permanence delta.

objects.label: Wooden Slat Pent-Roof Awning
objects.biomeSkins: Timber host matches the biome wall-material wood family: grassland=oak, forest/taiga=pine/cedar, dense_forest=dark-stained mossy slat (climate-default mossy), desert=sun-cracked split timber, volcanic=charred slat, mystic=carved rune slat. Drops in treeless biomes (steppe, tundra, arctic) in favour of cloth_market_awning.
objects.notes: NO wind_sway: a rigid wood pent-roof is NOT suspended cloth, so per the calibration rule it stays static even though it shares the awning category. Same physical role (rain hood over door/window) but the suspension property is absent.

objects.label: Fringed Shop Canopy
objects.biomeSkins: role-glyph variants carry the trade colour (baker=cream, butcher=red-white, dyer=multi); per biome the palette desaturates in harsh-sun biomes (sun_faded default) and gains snow_cap fold in cold biomes. mystic=enchanted shimmer fringe (light emissive added).
objects.notes: Suspended cloth with a hanging fringe → wind_sway. Wider 3-tile span suits a full shopfront; fit=span stretches the kit to the resolved window/door run width.

application.when: biome:grassland; building_role in {inn, tavern, shop, smith, bakery, apothecary, general_store, guildhall}; socket=above_door or a wall_bracket slot; one trade sign per public-facing entrance
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.9 on commercial/civic frontage; 1 per entrance

objects.label: Swinging Trade Sign
objects.biomeSkins: role-glyph drives the painted device (boot=cobbler, anvil=smith, sheaf=baker, tankard=tavern, mortar=apothecary). Per biome the board host changes: forest=carved pine, fieldstone-heavy biomes=slate plaque, desert=bleached driftwood-grey, volcanic=iron-faced, mystic=glowing glyph board (emissive added, becomes light-bearing). Cold biomes get climate-default snow_cap on the top edge. Drops only in unsettled wilderness with no trades.
objects.notes: Hybrid: PixelLab board sprite + code shader-sway because it hangs from a bracket/hook → SUSPENDED → wind_sway applies. NO interact verb — a sign is read, not operated. The bracket it hangs from is a separate D3_wall_brackets object (see attach there).

objects.label: Projecting Board Sign
objects.biomeSkins: Same role-glyph trade devices as the swinging sign; board host follows biome wood/stone family. Rigidly bolted variant for windier biomes (steppe, mountains, ocean) where a swinging sign would be impractical.
objects.notes: NO wind_sway: this board is rigidly fixed flat against / projecting from the wall, bolted not hung — suspension property absent, so it stays static. Distinguishes the rigid mount from swinging_trade_sign purely by suspension.

objects.label: Wrought-Iron Silhouette Sign
objects.biomeSkins: Iron silhouette of the trade emblem; rust climate-default in wet biomes (swamp, river, ocean=rusted default), pristine in arid biomes, verdigris-copper variant in coastal salt air, mystic=etched-rune iron (emissive). Universal because iron-working exists everywhere a smith does.
objects.notes: Static: a rigid forged silhouette mounted to the wall. NOT destructible (wrought iron does not casually break and there is no honest broken_state — honest absence of the component). No light unless the mystic skin promotes it to emissive.

application.when: biome:grassland; building_role in {inn, tavern, guildhall, shrine, watch_post, wealthy_dwelling, shop}; socket=beside_door or wall_bracket; civic/hospitality/wealthy frontage; flanks entrances
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.6 per entrance-flank socket; typically paired either side of a door

objects.label: Iron-and-Glass Candle Lantern

interact.emits: diurnal on/off — lit at dusk, extinguished at dawn; toggling switches the emissive light + flame particle on/off

light.flicker: candle: low-amplitude warm flicker, ~6Hz noise, dims when broken_glass

objects.biomeSkins: Lit-multiplier raises intensity/radius in dark biomes (dense_forest, swamp, volcanic night, mystic) where lanterns are the dominant light. Cold biomes frost the glass (climate-default state adds frost overlay, slight cool tint). desert=brass-and-horn variant; mystic=cold-blue magical flame (#8ad0ff, no soot_grimed state); volcanic=ember-red flame. Frame rusts in wet biomes (rusted climate-default).
objects.notes: LIGHT component, not a lit:bool — body is the PixelLab sprite, the GLOW is procedural emissive routed into the GL lighting pass + a flame particle (never a 2D overlay). flicker_glow is the emissive loop on the light source. interact.verb=toggle because the on/off is diurnal. broken_glass kills the light (intensity→0) and writes a destruction delta.

objects.label: Bracket Oil Lamp

interact.emits: diurnal on/off; toggling lights/extinguishes the wick flame + glow

light.flicker: oil: steadier than candle, slow swell, soot-darkens when soot_grimed

objects.biomeSkins: Brighter, steadier light than candle — lit-multiplier strongest in dark biomes. desert/savanna=oil readily available (full default); arctic/tundra=fish/whale-oil variant; volcanic=naphtha brighter flame; mystic=everbright oil (never empties, no diurnal off). Wet biomes rust the bracket.
objects.notes: Hybrid light source (body sprite + emissive glow + flame particle through GL). content.fill axis (full/empty) is ORTHOGONAL to wear: an empty lamp cannot be lit even at dusk, so the toggle is gated on content. unlit_dry is the run-dry visual. interact.verb=toggle (diurnal).

objects.label: Strung Festival Lanterns

interact.emits: diurnal/festival on/off; toggling lights the row of paper lanterns

light.flicker: soft per-node flicker, phase-offset along the string

objects.biomeSkins: Festival/celebration dressing — D7 identity-kit gated (festive/wealthy settlements). Paper-lantern palette varies by biome culture; mystic=floating witchlight orbs (no string), volcanic=ember-jars. Drops in austere/abandoned roles.
objects.notes: Strung between two sockets → spline-assembly lays the line of lantern nodes (tile-along, repeating the kit along the run); SUSPENDED → wind_sway AND each node is a light → flicker_glow. Both anims apply because both the suspension and the emissive properties are present. Not individually destructible (a festoon, not a fragile vessel).

application.when: biome:grassland; any residential or civic building with windows; socket=window_jamb (paired left+right leaf per window); ground floor first, upper floors once vertical apertures render
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.5 of windows get shutters (poorer dwellings none); paired leaves per shuttered window

objects.label: Board-and-Batten Shutter

interact.motion: hinge swing about the jamb edge (constrained, ~95°)

objects.biomeSkins: Painted-shutter colour by regional culture; timber host follows biome wood family. Wet biomes → paint_faded/mossy default; arctic/tundra → heavy storm-shutter variant (snow_cap on sill); desert → sun-bleached cracked; volcanic → charred; mystic → rune-carved. hanging_loose climate-default in abandoned/storm-prone roles.
objects.notes: interact.verb=open_close — a CONSTRAINED HINGE (the calibration rule for open_close vs toggle). NO wind_sway: a shutter is rigid and hinge-constrained, not freely suspended. broken/hanging_loose are damage states; open_close still possible while weathered but blocked when broken.

objects.label: Louvred Shutter

interact.motion: hinge swing about the jamb edge (constrained, ~95°)

objects.biomeSkins: Slatted louvre for ventilation — favoured in hot biomes (savanna, tropical_forest, desert, swamp) as the climate-appropriate default; cold biomes prefer the solid board_batten_shutter (louvred drops or rarefies there). mystic=carved filigree louvre.
objects.notes: Same open_close constrained-hinge affordance as the board shutter; differs only in art (ventilating slats) and biome bias. Static — rigid hinge, not suspended.

application.when: biome:grassland; building_role in {dwelling, inn, cottage, wealthy_dwelling}; socket=window_sill / under_window; maintained/inhabited dwellings (skipped on abandoned); ground-floor windows first
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.4 of sills on inhabited dwellings; 1 box per shuttered/open window

objects.label: Timber Window Flower Box
objects.biomeSkins: content season states reskin the planted flora to the biome's bloom catalog (grassland=wildflowers, savanna=dry grasses, tropical_forest=orchids, desert=succulents, arctic/tundra=snow_capped or empty default, mystic=glowing blossoms with faint emissive, volcanic=ash-tolerant red blooms, swamp=mossy/fern). Box timber host follows biome wood family. snow_capped is the climate-default winter/cold-biome content state.
objects.notes: content.axis=season (the seasonal/yield axis, orthogonal to box wear): blooming/full_green/empty/withered/snow_capped track season + maintenance, NOT damage. NO interact (you don't operate a flower box). NO wind_sway on the box itself — it is a rigid sill-mounted vessel; any flora-sway is the planted flora's own anim, not the box's.

objects.label: Terracotta Wall Planter
objects.biomeSkins: Fired-clay half-pot bracketed to the wall between windows; biome bloom reskin as above. Cold biomes frost-crack the terracotta (cracked default); desert=glazed-tile pot variant; mystic=rune-glazed.
objects.notes: Same season-content vessel rule as the timber box, but fired clay so it gains a 'cracked' intermediate damage state before 'broken'. Rigid → static, no interact.

application.when: biome:grassland; any building that hosts a hanging sign or wall lantern; a bracket is placed as the MOUNT whenever a swinging_trade_sign or hanging lantern socket is chosen (composition support)
application.chanceOrDensity: 1 per hanging-sign or hanging-lantern socket (paired with the child object)

objects.label: Wrought-Iron Mounting Bracket
objects.biomeSkins: Iron scrollwork; rusted climate-default in wet biomes (swamp, river, ocean), pristine in arid, verdigris-copper in salt-coastal, mystic=etched-rune iron (faint emissive), volcanic=blackened forged. Universal — brackets exist anywhere smithing does.
objects.notes: attach component: this bracket is a COMPOSITE host — holds a swinging_trade_sign or a hanging lantern in its hook_eye slot. The child (sign/lantern) is a SEPARATE object with its own destructible/light; the bracket itself is rigid wrought iron (static, not destructible — honest absence of a fragile broken_state). This realises the design-doc bracket→lantern composition example.

objects.label: Carved Timber Corbel Bracket
objects.biomeSkins: Carved corbel matching the biome wood family; dense_forest=mossy default, desert=sun-cracked, mystic=rune-carved. Lighter-duty than iron — holds signs but not heavy lanterns (slots omit lantern).
objects.notes: attach.holds is narrower than the iron bracket (signs only — a wooden corbel won't carry a heavy lit lantern safely). Unlike the iron bracket this timber one IS destructible (wood splits), so it carries broken_state + debris.

application.when: biome:grassland; any building with a door; socket=on_door (knocker/handle centred) or door_jamb (nameplate); knockers/nameplates skew to civic, guild, inn, wealthy roles; handles universal
avoid: door_path travel (mounted ON the leaf, moves with it)
application.chanceOrDensity: handle ~0.8 of doors; knocker ~0.3 (formal frontages); nameplate ~0.2 (named establishments)

objects.label: Iron Door Knocker
objects.biomeSkins: Knocker device shape varies by culture (ring, lion-head, hand-of-fatima); rusted in wet biomes, polished on wealthy frontages, mystic=glyph knocker (faint emissive), volcanic=obsidian-faced. Universal.
objects.notes: interact.verb=momentary — a ONE-SHOT action (the calibration rule: momentary = knocker/bell-pull), emits a knock_sound event and returns to rest, unlike toggle (persistent state) or open_close (constrained travel). NOT destructible (solid iron, no honest broken_state). Static body — only the momentary action animates.

objects.label: Door Handle & Latch
objects.biomeSkins: Iron/brass/bronze handle by settlement wealth; rusted in wet biomes, polished on wealthy frontages. mystic=rune-etched, volcanic=blackened iron. Universal.
objects.notes: NO interact verb of its OWN: the latch is the visual affordance of the building's door (the door's own open_close lives on the base building, not on this dressing prop). It is decorative/identifying dressing only. Static, not destructible (solid hardware).

objects.label: Engraved Nameplate
objects.biomeSkins: Brass/slate/carved-wood plate by biome material family; role-glyph engraves the establishment glyph (guild crest, family sigil). mystic=glowing engraved runes (emissive). Skews to named establishments — drops on anonymous huts.
objects.notes: Identifying plaque beside/on the door; read, not operated → no interact. role-glyph variant carries the establishment identity (feeds D7 identity-kit). Static, non-destructible (small fixed plate, honest absence of break/light).

application.when: biome:grassland; building_role in {guildhall, inn, shrine, market_stall, town_hall} OR festival/celebration settlement state; socket=facade-wide hang or above_door; civic/festive frontage
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.5 on civic/guild frontage; festival D7 raises across a whole street

objects.label: Hanging Heraldic Banner
objects.biomeSkins: role-glyph carries the guild/house/shrine device and tincture; per biome the cloth host shifts (felt in cold biomes with snow_cap fold, light silk in tropical, oiled canvas coastal). sun_faded climate-default in harsh-sun biomes; mystic=enchanted shimmer banner (emissive). Drops in roleless wilderness huts.
objects.notes: Long vertical hanging cloth → SUSPENDED → wind_sway (the suspension rule). Hybrid: PixelLab cloth sprite + code shader-sway. Destructible (fabric) → tatters. role-glyph makes it a primary identity carrier for D7.

objects.label: Triangle Pennant Bunting
objects.biomeSkins: Festive triangle pennants strung along the facade; colour palette per culture; cold biomes get heavier felt pennants, mystic=glowing pennants (emissive). Festival/celebration D7-gated; drops on austere/abandoned roles.
objects.notes: Strung between sockets → spline-assembly lays the catenary line (tile-along, repeating the pennant kit along the run); SUSPENDED cloth → wind_sway. Not individually destructible (a strung festoon, degrades as a whole via the sun_faded/tattered states).

application.when: biome:grassland; building_role in {dwelling, inn, shrine, cottage} AND (inhabited/maintained OR festival/seasonal celebration); socket=on_door (wreath) or facade-wide hang (garland)
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.3 of inhabited dwelling doors; festival/season D7 raises garlands across frontages

objects.label: Foliage Door Wreath
objects.biomeSkins: Foliage reskins to the biome bloom/flora catalog (grassland=wheat-and-wildflower, forest=evergreen, desert=dried-grass-and-succulent, tropical=palm-and-orchid, arctic/tundra=snow_frosted default, mystic=glowing-bloom wreath with faint emissive, volcanic=ash-resilient red). snow_frosted is the cold-biome climate-default content state.
objects.notes: content.axis=season (fresh/blooming/dried/snow_frosted) — a seasonal living-foliage axis, orthogonal to nothing else here. Mounted FLAT on the door leaf (not suspended/dangling) → static, NO wind_sway. Not destructible (foliage withers via content states, not a break delta).

objects.label: Draped Festoon Garland
objects.biomeSkins: Draped foliage swag strung between sockets; biome bloom reskin as the wreath; festival/season D7-gated; mystic=glowing garland (emissive), cold biomes snow_frosted default. Drops in austere/abandoned roles.
objects.notes: Draped/strung between two sockets → spline-assembly lays the catenary swag (tile-along), and being SUSPENDED → wind_sway (unlike the flat door_wreath which is mounted rigid). content.season axis tracks the living foliage. Not break-destructible (degrades via content states).

fields.crossBiomeNotes: D3 wall attachments are socket-anchored props that paint into the building silhouette at the flat baseline depth (mechanism B) and inherit GL lighting/CRT/day-night for free; lit and strung pieces add emissive/particle into the GL lighting pass (never a 2D overlay). The grassland section is authored concrete; the other 20 biomes are reached by biomeSkins, NOT new categories: (1) MATERIAL-HOST SWAP — timber/iron/cloth hosts follow each biome's wall-material wood/stone/metal family (the building-materials.json hosts), so a swinging sign becomes carved-pine in forest, slate in fieldstone biomes, driftwood-grey on the coast. (2) CLIMATE-DEFAULT STATE — cold biomes (arctic, tundra, taiga, mountains) default cloth/foliage to snow_capped/snow_frosted and frost glass; wet biomes (swamp, river, ocean, deep_ocean) default iron to rusted and cloth to mildew/paint_faded; arid biomes (desert, savanna, steppe) default cloth/paint to sun_faded and bias louvred shutters over solid. (3) FLORA-RESKIN — flower boxes, wreaths and garlands repaint their planted content to each biome's bloom catalog. (4) LIT-MULTIPLIER — dark biomes (dense_forest, swamp, volcanic-night, mystic) raise wall-lantern intensity/radius because lanterns dominate their light budget. (5) MAGICAL VARIANTS — mystic (and volcanic) promote certain static props to emissive (rune signs, glowing wreaths, witchlight festoons, cold-blue flames). (6) DROP CONDITIONS — commercial/festive categories (awnings, bunting, festival lights, garlands) drop on roleless wilderness and abandoned buildings; treeless biomes drop wood-slat awnings/timber brackets in favour of cloth/iron. Affordance rule discipline held throughout: wind_sway ONLY on suspended cloth/strung/hanging pieces (cloth awnings, hanging signs, banners, bunting, garlands) and NOT on rigid mounts (wood-slat awnings, projecting/iron signs, shutters, brackets, flower boxes, door furniture, flat door wreaths); light is a full component (color/radius/intensity/diurnal/flicker, body-sprite + GL emissive) only on actual light sources, never a lit:bool; interact verbs are precise — open_close for the constrained shutter hinge, toggle for the diurnal lantern on/off, momentary for the one-shot knocker, and null where a prop is merely read or where the verb belongs to the base building (door handle); content uses the season/fill axis for vessels and living foliage orthogonal to wear; attach makes the wall brackets composite hosts holding signs/lanterns; no coverage component appears because D3 props are discrete sockets, not D0–D2 surfaces.

application.when: biome:grassland; socket:above_door on the entry face (south preferred); building_role any dwelling/inn/shop; settlement_tier hamlet+; honestly skips wealth-gating (no sim source) — applies by role not wealth
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.35 of dwellings carry an entry porch; 0.7 for inn/tavern role (a porch is the social threshold)

objects.label: Posted timber entry porch
objects.biomeSkins: Material host follows the building wall material: timber_frame/wattle_daub host → oak-post porch; fieldstone host → stone-pier porch with timber roof; cob host → cob-pier porch under a deep thatch eave. Across biomes the posts re-skin to the biome's dominant wall vernacular (forest/dense_forest → round-log porch; tropical_forest → bamboo+palm-thatch verandah; beach/shallow_water → driftwood-plank porch; ocean/deep_ocean → tarred-timber stilt porch; lake/river → cedar/board porch; desert/savanna → adobe-pier ramada; steppe/hills/mountains → fieldstone+timber; tundra/taiga/arctic → heavy-log storm porch, climate-default state=snow_capped via content; volcanic → basalt-pier porch with ash-fade weathering; mystic → rune-carved post variant, faint emissive trim). Roof piece inherits the building's roof material where available.
objects.notes: A porch is a real built structure: it OWNS depth and a collision footprint (3x2 tiles projecting from the entry face) and packs into the F2 SPRITE_FLOATS pool with its own pivotY so the player and flora sort correctly under/around its eave. It anchors at above_door and the roof piece overhangs the doorway; the floor tile is walkable. Because it casts a real ground shadow (procedural shadow codeEffect) it must be excluded from the entry door_path claim. attach makes it a host for D3 signs/lanterns and D5/D6 ground props — composites resolve as separate lootable children. Destructible because timber structures collapse; the broken_state writes an object-permanence delta.

objects.label: Stone-pier entry porch
objects.biomeSkins: Bound to fieldstone wall host in grassland; reads as squared lime-mortared piers carrying a low timber-shingle roof. Other biomes swap the pier stone to the biome's masonry vernacular (river → millstone ashlar, lake → glacial fieldstone, mountains/hills → quarried block, desert → adobe, volcanic → basalt, beach → coral block). Cold biomes default state=mossy_overgrown→snow on the roof via the host roof material; mystic adds a faint emissive rune on the keystone.
objects.notes: Heavier masonry variant of the entry porch for fieldstone (wealthier) dwellings. Same own-depth + collision footprint as the timber porch; the stone piers are the load path so the broken_state is rubble rather than splintered planks. Sorts via pivotY in the SPRITE_FLOATS pool; excluded from door_path claim.

application.when: biome:grassland; socket:wall_corner or between_windows on a load-bearing face; building_role inn/hall/wealthy-dwelling/shop with an overhang or upper jetty; settlement_tier village+
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.2 of buildings; near-1.0 where an upper storey jetties out over the ground floor (a post is then structurally honest, not decorative)

objects.label: Oak support post
objects.biomeSkins: Material host = building wall: timber_frame/wattle_daub → carved dark-oak post; cob → squat earthen pier; fieldstone → dressed stone column. Per biome the post re-skins to the wall vernacular (forest → round-log post, tropical_forest → bamboo bundle, beach/ocean → driftwood/tarred-timber piling, desert/savanna → adobe column, mountains → stone column, volcanic → basalt column, mystic → carved rune-column with faint emissive seams). Cold biomes carry snow on the bracket via content=snow_capped.
objects.notes: A free-standing structural post carrying an upper-storey jetty or porch lintel. Slim 1x2 footprint but it DOES collide (you walk around it) and owns depth — packs into SPRITE_FLOATS with pivotY at its base. Anchored at wall_corner or between_windows; the post_top_bracket slot hosts a D3 lantern or sign so a porch corner becomes a lit threshold. Honest structure: appears where geometry actually overhangs.

objects.label: Dressed stone column
objects.biomeSkins: Grassland fieldstone host → honey-sandstone column with a simple carved capital. Wealthier/civic re-skin across biomes (river → gorge-slate column, mountains → granite, desert → sandstone, volcanic → polished basalt, mystic → glowing crystal-veined column with emissive capital). Drops on biomes with no masonry tradition (drop: ocean, deep_ocean, shallow_water unless lighthouse/civic role).
objects.notes: Taller civic/wealthy column (3 tiles) for halls, shrines and prosperous houses. Same own-depth + collision discipline; the toppled_column broken_state leaves rollable column drums as debris (object-permanence delta). Anchored at wall_corner of a portico or hall facade.

application.when: biome:grassland; socket:window_sill on floor>=1 (upper storeys only); building_role inn/townhouse/wealthy-dwelling; DEPENDENCY: requires the facade to render floor>=1 apertures — honestly absent on single-storey buildings and until upper-storey windows draw
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.15 of multi-storey buildings; 0.4 for inn/townhouse role on the street face

objects.label: Projecting timber balcony
objects.biomeSkins: Material host = wall: timber_frame → carved-bracket oak balcony; cob/wattle_daub → simpler plank balcony on timber brackets; fieldstone → corbelled stone balcony with timber deck. Per biome re-skin to vernacular (forest → log-bracket balcony, tropical_forest → bamboo verandah balcony with deep eave, beach/ocean → driftwood/tarred-plank balcony, desert/savanna → adobe corbel balcony, mountains → stone corbel, mystic → rune-bracket balcony, faint emissive underglow). Cold biomes pile snow on the deck via content=snow_capped.
objects.notes: Projects out from an upper-storey window_sill: it OWNS depth, casts a shadow on the ground floor below, and creates an overhang the player passes under (its collision is the deck volume up at floor>=1, not at ground). Spans the window width (fit:span). Strong vertical-placement dependency — needs floor>=1 apertures to render; declared honestly absent until then. attach hosts a railing run (D4_railings), lanterns, flower boxes (D2) and potted plants (D5). Destructible: a broken balcony is a classic decay read and writes a delta.

application.when: biome:grassland; socket:balcony_rail_run / porch_floor_edge / exterior_stair_run / roof_edge; gated on a host structure existing (balcony, porch, stair, parapet) — never floats free; settlement_tier hamlet+
application.chanceOrDensity: near-1.0 along any balcony/stair edge (a railing is a safety implication of the host); 0.5 along porch floor edges

objects.label: Turned-baluster timber railing
objects.biomeSkins: Grassland timber_frame/wattle_daub/cob host → turned oak balusters; fieldstone host → carved stone balustrade variant. Per biome: forest → split-rail/log balusters, tropical_forest → bamboo lattice rail, beach/ocean → rope-and-driftwood rail, desert/savanna → adobe parapet with carved openings, mountains/hills → stone balustrade, lake/river → cedar rail, cold biomes → heavy timber rail (snow_capped via content), mystic → glowing-rune balusters, volcanic → wrought-basalt rail. Some hosts swap turned-wood to wrought-iron where the biome's metalwork vernacular exists (river/mountains).
objects.notes: A kit piece repeated along a run (fit:tile-along) — the run length is read from the host structure's edge slot (balcony_rail_run, exterior_stair_run, porch_floor_edge, roof parapet). It NEVER places free-floating; the category gates on a host. Each piece owns a thin collision strip and shares the host's depth/pivot. Promoted broken state lets a run show a gap where a baluster snapped (delta-written). rail_post_top hosts a lantern at run ends.

application.when: biome:grassland; socket:above_door (entry on a raised plinth) or a wall face leading to an upper external door; building_role workshop/store/townhouse with an upper entrance or raised floor; settlement_tier hamlet+
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.25 of buildings on a plinth/slope; near-1.0 where an upper-storey external door exists

objects.label: Timber entry stair
objects.biomeSkins: Grassland timber host → oak-tread stair; cob/wattle_daub → timber stair on an earthen ramp; fieldstone → mortared stone steps. Per biome: forest → log-tread stair, tropical_forest → bamboo stair, beach/ocean → driftwood/dock stair over piling, lake/river → cedar dock-stair, desert/savanna → adobe steps, mountains/hills → cut-stone stair, cold biomes → heavy timber stair (snow_capped via content), volcanic → basalt steps, mystic → floating-rune steps with faint emissive risers.
objects.notes: A real walkable stair with own depth + a stepped collision footprint (2x2) projecting from the entry face; packs into SPRITE_FLOATS with pivotY at its base tread. Excluded from the door_path claim (it IS the door path). exterior_stair_run slot hands a railing run to D4_railings; stair_newel_bottom hosts a lantern. Destructible — a broken tread is a strong abandonment read and writes a delta. (Climbing the stair to an upper external door is an interior-walk-in seam, deferred per design.)

objects.label: Stone entry steps
objects.biomeSkins: Grassland fieldstone host → lime-mortared stone steps. Re-skins to biome masonry (river → slate steps, mountains → granite, desert → sandstone, volcanic → basalt, beach → coral-block steps). Cold biomes default mossy_overgrown→snow via host; mystic adds emissive worn glyphs in the tread centres.
objects.notes: Low masonry steps (2x1) up to a raised threshold — the durable counterpart to the timber stair for fieldstone dwellings. Own depth + collision; the cracked_steps broken_state is a slow-decay read writing a delta. Excluded from door_path claim; flanks host potted plants (D5).

application.when: biome:grassland; socket:above_door / between_windows / porch_eave on a sunny (south) face; building_role dwelling/inn/garden-house; settlement_tier hamlet+; reads warmer with D2 surface-growth vines climbing it
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.2 of dwellings on a south face; 0.5 for inn/tavern (a vine pergola is the beer-garden read)

objects.label: Timber pergola frame
objects.biomeSkins: Grassland timber host → oak pergola; per biome re-skin (forest → rustic log pergola, tropical_forest → bamboo pergola, beach/ocean → driftwood arbour, desert/savanna → adobe-post ramada with reed lattice, mountains → stone-post pergola, cold biomes → bare heavy-timber arbour, snow_capped via content). The CLIMBING FLORA on it reskins to the biome bloom catalog (grassland → wild_lavender/cornflower vine read; tropical_forest → passion_flower/heliconia; desert → desert_rose; mystic → moonpetal/aether_bloom with faint emissive). Volcanic → ash-bare frame. content season states drive leafy/blooming/bare with the biome's flora colour.
objects.notes: An open lattice frame over a path or seating area — own depth + light collision on its posts (you walk under the beams). It is the structural HOST that D2 surface-growth vines climb (attach holds D2_climbing_vine), so the affordance split is honest: D4 owns the frame + collision, D2 owns the grown vine spline. content uses the SEASON axis (not wear) for leafy/blooming/bare, orthogonal to the weathered wear states. Spans an entry/garden run (fit:span).

objects.label: Wall-mounted trellis panel
objects.biomeSkins: Grassland → oak lattice panel; per biome re-skin to vernacular lattice (tropical_forest → split-cane, beach → driftwood, desert → reed). Climbing flora reskins to the biome bloom catalog as the pergola; cold biomes default bare; mystic gives a faint emissive frame.
objects.notes: A flatter trellis fixed against a wall face between windows — minimal depth (sits close to the wall) but still a B socket-prop with a thin collision strip, distinct from the D2 vine that grows ON it. Hosts a D2_climbing_vine via attach. season content drives the leaf/bloom read with the biome flora colour; weathered states are the orthogonal wear axis.

application.when: biome:grassland; socket:wall_corner / blank_wall_run on a side or rear face (never the street face); building_role farmstead/smith/workshop/dwelling-with-yard; settlement_tier hamlet+
application.chanceOrDensity: 0.3 of farmstead/workshop buildings; 0.6 for smith (a fuel/tool lean-to is a working-yard read)

objects.label: Timber lean-to shed
objects.biomeSkins: Material host = wall: timber_frame/wattle_daub → plank lean-to under a thatch or shingle slope; cob → cob-and-thatch lean-to; fieldstone → low stone lean-to with timber roof. Roof piece inherits the building's roof material.
